findings.title: No test for a preview update on an unknown conversation, or one already first
findings.failure_scenario: Two guards have no test. (1) AppFeature.swift:31 lets a tap on an id that is not in the list return without presenting a thread. (2) AppFeature.swift:36-37 lets lastMessageChanged for an unknown conversationID return without changing anything. Nothing sends an unknown id, so a mutant that presents a thread or inserts a conversation for an unknown id still passes. The claimed duplication mutant can't happen: conversations is an IdentifiedArray, so insert(_:at:) of an existing id is a no-op and the list can't hold the same id twice. If the remove is dropped, delegateUpdatesPreview already fails, because convA stays second with its old preview.
findings.evidence: AppFeatureTests.swift:34 taps only "a", which is in the list. AppFeatureTests.swift:43/50 sends lastMessageChanged only for "a", which sits at index 1. No test sends an id missing from the list, so the else branches at AppFeature.swift:31 and :36-37 never run.
findings.fix: Add tests: a lastMessageChanged for an unknown conversationID leaves the list unchanged, one for the already-first conversation keeps the list length, and a tap on an unknown id leaves thread nil.
findings.verification_note: Read AppFeature.swift and AppFeatureTests.swift in the worktree. The two unknown-id guards (lines 31 and 36-37) are never exercised: both tests use ids that are in the list, so the gap is real. The test-store tests are exhaustive, so a new test would pin these branches. The 'already-first is duplicated' part does not hold: IdentifiedArray dedupes by id, and dropping the remove is already caught by delegateUpdatesPreview. This is a test-coverage gap with no wrong behavior today, so it stays minor (no-harm-yet).

notes:
AppFeature: list(.conversationTapped(id)) sets state.thread = ThreadFeature.State(conversation:) (unknown id does nothing); thread(.presented(.delegate(.lastMessageChanged(m)))) sets that conversation's lastMessage and moves it to index 0. AppView uses navigationDestination(item: $store.scope(state: \.thread, action: \.thread)) to ThreadView. Tests: tapOpensThread, delegateUpdatesPreview in AppFeatureTests.swift.
